title: Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in pp collisions at 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
authors: ATLAS Collaboration
gist: ATLAS looks for a rare, isotropic particle pattern expected from QCD instantons and sees a 3.5 sigma excess: suggestive, not a discovery.
explain: Question: QCD instantons, tunnelling events between topologically distinct vacua, are predicted but have never been seen at a collider.
Signature: a low-mass instanton decays into many soft charged particles spread isotropically in its rest frame, unlike ordinary minimum-bias events.
Method: ATLAS uses 1.6 nb⁻¹ of very-low-pileup 13 TeV data, feeds track angular variables into a classifier, and models the background from data and reweighted Monte Carlo.
Result: an excess of isotropic low-mass events at 3.5σ. A first hint that needs independent confirmation and a careful look at background modelling.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data: prompt J/psi cross-section measurements in pp and peripheral PbPb collisions
authors: Z. Cui, Z. Wang, G. Bauer et al.
gist: An AI coding agent, with physicists reviewing each step, reanalyses public CMS data on J/psi production and gets results broadly consistent with the published ones.

title: Seeing through the fog: astrophysical priors and the evidence for new physics in pulsar timing arrays
authors: T. Bringmann, C. Gordon, C. Tasillo
gist: Checks whether the pulsar-timing gravitational-wave signal really requires new physics once black-hole-binary models and updated priors are used.

title: Fuzzy Dark Matter as a diffractive barrier: wave-optics signatures of ultralight fields on lensed gravitational waves
authors: M. Tamta, H. G. Choi, D. Blas et al.
gist: Ultralight dark-matter halos may leave small, frequency-dependent distortions in lensed gravitational waves that future detectors could see.
explain: Setup: ultralight dark-matter halos are granular, because the wave-like field interferes with itself.
Effect: in the wave-optics regime these granules act as a diffraction grating for gravitational waves, adding frequency-dependent modulations to ordinary lensing.
Size: about 1% for moderately lensed signals, and above 10% near critical curves or for Type II images.
Payoff: for massive black-hole binaries seen by LISA, the effect is detectable around m ≈ 10⁻²¹ eV, giving either a smoking gun or new bounds on the boson mass.

title: Steerability in top quark decays at the LHC
authors: T. Han, N. McGinnis, S. Salamat et al.
gist: Estimates how well the LHC and its high-luminosity upgrade could detect quantum steering in top-quark pairs.
explain: Context: top-quark pairs carry their spin correlations into the decay products, which already allowed the LHC to observe entanglement.
Concept: EPR steering is a stronger quantum correlation than entanglement but weaker than Bell nonlocality.
Method: the authors estimate the sensitivity with both the decay and the kinematic methods, in the semileptonic and dileptonic channels, at high boost and near threshold.
Result: with 139 fb⁻¹, steering in boosted tt̄ could be established at 7.7σ (semileptonic); an optimised cut near threshold gives about 7σ, and HL-LHC sharpens the precision.

title: Cost-optimized detectors for the GUT-scale QCD axion
authors: J. N. Benabou, J. W. Foster, B. R. Safdi
gist: Estimates the cheapest laboratory experiment able to probe a heavier QCD axion; a large toroidal detector comes out as the most cost-effective design.

title: Capturing ultralight dark matter around black holes
authors: S. Bottaro, V. Firsov, G. Perez et al.
gist: Self-interacting ultralight dark matter can build dense halos around black holes, which caps how massive the clouds around spinning black holes can grow.

title: Leading axion sensitivity with interstellar medium optical line emission
authors: R. K. Leane, G. Sundaresan
gist: Optical hydrogen emission from the Leo T galaxy is used to set strong new limits on light axion dark matter.
explain: Idea: axion dark matter decaying to photons or electrons can excite or ionise neutral hydrogen in galaxies.
Signature: the hydrogen then emits Hα light at a fixed atomic wavelength, whatever the axion mass is.
Data: Very Large Telescope observations of the gas-rich dwarf galaxy Leo T.
Result: leading limits on axion–photon and axion–electron couplings for eV–GeV masses, which also disfavour axion explanations of JWST's early supermassive black holes.

title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited
authors: E. Vitchev
gist: Revisits conserved charges in free bosonic conformal field theories and checks them with exact arithmetic.

title: A Positive Metric on Four-Dimensional QFTs
authors: T. Hartman, G. Mathys, A. Stergiou
gist: Extends a known metric on the space of quantum field theories beyond perturbation theory and argues it is non-negative, implying a strong form of the a-theorem.
explain: Background: Jack and Osborn defined a metric on the space of 4d QFTs that, in perturbation theory, controls the flow of the a-anomaly.
Step: the authors build a non-perturbative version of this metric from the three-point function ⟨O 𝓔 O⟩, with 𝓔 the averaged null energy.
Key tool: decomposing under null rotations around the light ray turns positivity into a condition at each impact parameter, guaranteed by the averaged null energy condition.
Consequence: the ANEC implies the strong a-theorem, with an explicit function that decreases monotonically along the RG flow.

title: Direct inference of cosmological mass growth via timing of black hole - pulsar binaries
authors: K. S. Croker, G. B. Bowling, C. Cain et al.
gist: Uses pulsar timing in a globular cluster to test whether black holes grow together with the expanding universe.

title: Spinning particle dynamics around a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity
authors: Karshiboev, Turimov, Usanov et al.
gist: Studies how spinning test particles move around a smoothed-out black hole from conformal gravity and whether it differs from standard Schwarzschild.

title: Probing the Graviton Mass through the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background Last-Scattering Surface
authors: H. Zhang, Z. Qiu, S. Wang et al.
gist: A nonzero graviton mass would change the angular pattern of the cosmic gravitational-wave background, offering a way to constrain it.

title: Ohmic warm inflation
authors: A. Ghoshal, A. Strumia
gist: Shows that the 'warm little inflation' model is anomalous and cannot sustain its thermal bath, and proposes anomaly-free replacements based on U(1) gauge groups with a Wilson-line inflaton.
abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflato

title: Dijet production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at NNLO+PS accuracy
authors: F. König, M. Wiesemann, G. Zanderighi
gist: First event generator with NNLO QCD accuracy matched to a parton shower for lepton collisions, applied to dijets; relevant for LEP data and future e+e- colliders.
abstract: We present the first complete Monte Carlo event generator with next-to-next-to-leading order QCD accuracy for lepton collisions. The approach is based on a new formulation of the MiNNLO formalism and is applied to dijet production. Starting from the resummation of the three-jet resolution variable $y_3$, we present the corresponding MiNNLO master formula and implement it within the Powheg framework. We discuss phenomenological results relevant for LEP and future electron-positron colliders.

title: Probing Compressed Dark Sectors at a Muon Collider through Dilepton Signatures and Machine Learning
authors: M. Belfkir, A. Hmissou, L. Rahili
gist: Studies how well a muon collider could find inert-doublet dark matter with compressed spectra, using boosted decision trees on a dilepton signature.
abstract: The inert doublet model (IDM), a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM), provides a scalar dark matter (DM) candidate that belongs to the additional Higgs doublet. The model faces challenges in achieving the correct relic abundance for compressed spectra and DM masses in the high-mass range. In this work we investigate the prospects of detecting dark matter candidates at future high-energy muon colliders. Focusing on the process $\mu^+ \mu^- \to AH$ with subsequent decay $A \to H Z^*$ and $Z^* \to \ell^+\ell^-$, we explore the sensitivity of machine learning techniques, specifically Boosted Decision Trees (BDT) and XGBoost, to distinguish the signal from Standard Model backgrounds. We

title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
authors: F. Chang, S. Wan, S. Zhou
gist: Analytic method to build the curved positivity cones of SMEFT quartic gauge couplings, also usable to infer which UV models sit on their boundaries.
abstract: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: Zeroing in on BSM at Colliders
authors: C. Cesarotti, M. McCullough, M. Riembau
gist: Explains when interference between light and heavy states makes an amplitude vanish well below the heavy threshold, and what the resulting dip says about UV physics at colliders.
abstract: Destructive interference between light and heavy dynamics can produce a zero in the amplitude which, for strongly coupled UV completions, lies parametrically below the heavy threshold. We identify under which assumptions this parametrically light zero exists, and when it admits an effective field theory description. We study how absorptive effects and helicity structure affect the existence of the zero and turn it into a dip. When the dip is kinematically accessible, we show how its position, depth, and curvature constrain the UV dynamics. Collider examples illustrate the importance of interference in indirect searches and the information available when the zero is kinematically accessible.

title: Energy and Charge Transmission at Conformal Interfaces: Relations and Bounds
authors: Y. Furuta, Y. Kusuki, T. Onagi, et al.
gist: Derives an exact relation between energy and charge transmission across WZW conformal interfaces, which rules out complete energy transmission between unequal levels.
abstract: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an exact relation between the energy and charge transmission coefficients, $c_{LR}=2(\dim G)k_{LR}/(k_L+k_R+2h^\vee)$. Together with positivity of outgoing energy, this relation excludes complete energy transmission at unequal levels. With additional bulk degrees of freedom, the equality is replaced by bounds controlled by the coset central charges. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other si

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
authors: S. Aoki, L. Pinol, Z. Qin, et al.
gist: Gives an analytic formula for the primordial bispectrum from triple exchange of massive scalars, a key ingredient of cosmological collider signals.
abstract: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple a

title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
authors: R. Dempsey, A. Glück, S. Pufu, et al.
gist: Uses tensor networks to simulate real-time e+e- collisions of solitons in the massive Schwinger model, showing the formation and breaking of a flux string.
abstract: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model. We work at $\theta = \pi$ and at a bare fermion mass exceeding the critical value; in this regime, there are two degenerate vacua, and the $e^+$ and $e^-$ particles are realized as soliton states interpolating between them. We carefully explain how to find and characterize such soliton states using infinite tensor network methods, and then exhibit real-time simulations of their collisions. These collisions involve the formation of an energetic flux string, and we demonstrate that our final stat

title: Microscopic Cosmological Backreaction of an Ultralight Majoron Coupled to a Coherent Hidden Pseudo-Dirac Ensemble
authors: K. Cheon, S. Kang, J. Lee
gist: Builds a microscopic treatment of the cosmological backreaction from a pseudo-Dirac fermion ensemble coupled to an ultralight Majoron, including memory effects.
abstract: We develop a microscopic framework for the cosmological backreaction of a hidden pseudo-Dirac fermion ensemble derivatively coupled to an ultralight Majoron. Starting from the effective action, we derive the exact operator Ward identity for the pseudo-Dirac current and the associated microscopic energy-transfer law. For a thermal density matrix prepared at a finite initial time, we calculate the subsequent collisionless, linearized coherence response without assuming continued thermal equilibrium or introducing phenomenological dissipation. The finite-time retarded solution retains the initial boundary transient and nonlocal memory contribution, allowing us to assess the validity of the lead

title: A Relativistic Newton's Third Law for Binaries in Environments
authors: C. Dyson, A. Pound, D. D'Orazio, et al.
gist: Derives a relativistic Newton's third law for inspirals in matter environments, so orbital evolution follows from forces on the matter without solving for the perturbations.
abstract: We derive the relativistic form of Newton's Third Law governing the interaction between intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and surrounding relativistic matter fields. Working within a two-parameter expansion, we rewrite the evolution of the secondary's orbital elements in a form resembling the integrated forces acting on the environment, avoiding the need to calculate any gravitational perturbations sourced by the dynamical matter content. Using the retarded and advanced Green's functions, we obtain both instantaneous and orbit-averaged laws relating the rate of change of the secondary's orbital energy and angular momentum to that of the matter and the gravitational-wave fluxes a

title: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
authors: H. Wang, G. Ye, Y. Piao
gist: Argues that the post-peak 'tail' of early dark energy is an extra observable and affects how well it can ease the Hubble tension.
abstract: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the \emph{EDE tail}, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and $\alpha$-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations. Con

title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
authors: M. Yang, D. Yang, S. Hou, et al.
gist: Shows that compact stars can make self-interacting dark matter subhalos better strong lenses than cold dark matter ones, giving a new SIDM test.
abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGS

title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
authors: C. Witt, N. Pol
gist: Studies how a stochastic gravitational-wave background and a single supermassive black hole binary can confuse each other in pulsar timing array searches.
abstract: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. In this work, we analyze how the presence of this signal could affect our detection statistics for the GWB, and how the presence of the GWB can affect our search for the SMBHB system. We find tha

title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
authors: G. Aarts, D. Habibi, A. Ipp, et al.
gist: Uses gauge-equivariant diffusion models to sample lattice gauge theories, working in 2D U(2) and giving first results for 4D SU(3).
abstract: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
authors: L. Santos-Olmsted, R. Leane, C. Blanco, et al.
gist: Argues that xenon detectors should use the full single-electron 'dark-electron' rate, not severely cut data, to probe sub-GeV dark matter scattering on electrons, with much better reach.
abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-mo

title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
authors: C. Chiang, V. Tran
gist: Shows that gravity alone can produce superheavy dark matter, up to about 10^17 GeV, through graviton exchange in collisions of runaway bubble walls.
abstract: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/\beta$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/\beta)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/\beta)M_{\rm P}/\nu^2$, where $\nu$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.

title: A billion colour states: exact soft-gluon evolution beyond leading colour for many-jet QCD
authors: B. Chargeishvili
gist: New method for orthogonal colour bases that computes one-loop soft-gluon evolution exactly in full colour for many-jet QCD processes, keeping all colour interference.
abstract: We present a new method, and its implementation, for constructing orthogonal colour bases and computing colour factors for any process with quarks, antiquarks and gluons, and use it to compute one-loop soft-gluon evolution exactly in full colour, keeping all colour interference. Each basis vector is labelled, independently of $N_c$, by the sequence of colour representations that appear when the partons are coupled one at a time. We derive a closed formula for the norms of the basis vectors, and colour operators act only on the part of a label between the partons involved, through small tables. Basis vectors can therefore be generated and used one at a time, without listing the complete basis

title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
authors: R. Caliri, M. Kunkel, W. Porod
gist: Studies WZjj vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description; distribution tails deviate from the SM even when resonances lie beyond LHC reach.
abstract: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons.

title: Bring Your Own Instanton: Monopole Catalysis from Sourced SU(2) Instantons
authors: C. Csáki, L. Kiriliuk, Z. Liu, et al.
gist: Shows monopole catalysis of proton decay proceeds through new 'sourced SU(2) instantons' carrying unit instanton number, without exponential suppression.
abstract: We show that Rubakov-Callan catalysis of proton decay in the field of a 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole proceeds through "sourced SU(2) instantons", which are novel topological gauge configurations sourced by fermions and carrying unit instanton number. Unlike vacuum BPST instantons, these sourced instantons do not give rise to exponentially suppressed rates. We relate the winding number to the number of fermionic zero modes, suggesting an underlying index theorem for sourced instantons. We also calculate the closed-form expression for the leading-order correlator for fermion insertions both outside and inside the monopole core. Our results indicate that Rubakov-Callan catalysis is an IR effect w

title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
authors: T. Ahmed, S. Hasan
gist: Computes the 4PM scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin, including radiation reaction and spin-induced quadrupoles.
abstract: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.

title: The Gradient Structure of Perturbative RG Flows
authors: L. Benfatto, W. Pannell, A. Stergiou
gist: Shows perturbative RG flows are exact gradient flows to all orders, by removing the long-standing antisymmetric obstruction with a scheme choice via a sphere Ward identity.
abstract: Weyl consistency conditions show that perturbative renormalisation group flows in two, four and six dimensions are almost gradient flows. The obstruction is an antisymmetric contribution to the metric on the space of couplings, which has resisted removal since the work of Jack and Osborn more than 35 years ago. We show that a conformal Ward identity on the sphere allows it to be removed by a choice of scheme. The beta function is then the gradient of a potential $A$ with respect to a symmetric metric, to all orders in perturbation theory. The Ward identity gives this result in any dimension $d$, in theories with and without a Weyl anomaly. At leading order the metric is fixed by the two-poin

title: Lorentz-invariant fiducial decay selection for the ATLAS $H\to ZZ^{*}\to 4\ell$ STXS measurement
authors: ATLAS Collaboration
gist: Recasts ATLAS H→ZZ*→4ℓ STXS results into a Lorentz-invariant fiducial region, so EFT interpretations no longer depend on Standard Model decay acceptance.
abstract: ATLAS measurements of Higgs boson production-mode cross-sections and Simplified Template Cross Sections (STXS), $\sigma\cdot B$, in the $H\to ZZ^{*}\to 4\ell$ decay channel rely on selection factors that fold in a decay-side fiducial acceptance evaluated with Standard Model decay kinematics. In an effective-field-theory interpretation that acceptance depends on the Wilson coefficients themselves. We recast these production-side $\sigma\cdot B$ results into a single Lorentz-invariant fiducial (LIF) decay region defined by the $H\to 4\ell$ decay, absorbing the EFT-dependent fiducial acceptance into the signal parametrisation, while the remaining reconstruction-efficiency corrections are shown

title: Design of a Resonator Array Axion Haloscope and its Projected Sensitivity from 2 to 4 GHz
authors: ADMX Collaboration
gist: Presents the design of an 18-cavity ADMX haloscope with coherent signal combination and its projected sensitivity to QCD axion dark matter at 2-4 GHz.
abstract: The QCD axion is a dark matter (DM) candidate particle which can also solve the long-standing strong charge-parity problem. The Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) searches for resonantly-enhanced conversion of axion DM into photons in a strong magnetic field. Previous versions of the experiment probed most QCD axion DM from 2.7 $\mu$eV to 4.2 $\mu$eV, with ongoing and planned runs poised to cover up to 8 $\mu$eV (2 GHz). We present the design of a haloscope with 18 cavities 1 m in length read out using individual low-noise amplifier chains and digital coherent signal combination called ADMX extended frequency range (EFR). We discuss details on magnet and cryogenic infrastructure, cavity des

title: Quasinormal Modes and Excitation Factors of a Parity-Symmetric Beyond-Horndeski Black Hole
authors: R. Konoplya, M. Skvortsova
gist: Computes quasinormal modes and excitation factors of a beyond-Horndeski black hole using several cross-checked methods, relevant for ringdown tests of modified gravity.
abstract: We study scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations of an asymptotically flat black hole in parity-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. The quasinormal spectrum is computed with very-high-order WKB expansions and Pad\'e resummation, with Ces\`aro means used to diagnose internal convergence. The dominant modes are independently tested by time-domain evolution with Prony extraction and by Chebyshev pseudospectral collocation; the latter also provides systematic frequency scans in both the metric-scale and physical ADM-mass normalizations. Excitation factors are obtained separately from Green-function residues by complex-contour integration. In the fixed metric-scale normalization, approac

title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
authors: Y. Wang, J. Yao
gist: Studies how an extra Yukawa force from a binary companion changes ionization of ultralight-boson clouds around spinning black holes, altering orbital energy extraction.
abstract: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a

title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
authors: K. Boddy, J. Hazboun, K. Pardo
gist: Builds an optimal cross-correlation statistic combining pulsar timing and astrometric stellar deflections to search for a stochastic gravitational wave background.
abstract: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation stat

title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
authors: I. Chavez, A. Ghosh, C. Kelso, et al.
gist: Forecasts how LSST-discovered dwarf galaxies affect gamma-ray limits on dark matter annihilation, finding modest gains (below 20%) in most cases.
abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These resul

title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
authors: F. Huxhagen, D. López Nacir
gist: Uses NANOGrav 15-yr binary pulsar timing to constrain ultralight dark matter couplings (scalar and B-L vector) for masses 10^-23 to 10^-18 eV.
abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the

title: Dark vector meson effects on composite dark matter
authors: T. Abe, R. Sato, O. Semin, et al.
gist: Studies how dark vector mesons change the relic abundance and detection prospects of composite dark matter models.
abstract: We extend previous studies of $\mathcal{G}$-parity-odd dark pion dark matter in a QCD-like $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$ gauge theory with electroweakly interacting dark quarks to include the effects of $\rho$ mesons. We show that vector mesons can substantially affect relic abundance calculations through resonant enhancement, significantly affecting the conditions required to reproduce the observed relic abundance. Electroweak interactions further induce mixing between the dark $\rho$ mesons and Standard Model gauge bosons, opening new decay channels for the dark $\rho$ and modifying the effective interactions of the dark pions. We recast existing ATLAS and CMS searches to constrain the model, and per

title: Boosted energy-energy correlators in the small-acoplanarity limit
authors: B. Jobilal, Z. Kang, D. Padilla
gist: Computes boosted energy-energy correlators in the small-acoplanarity limit, relevant for precision jet substructure studies at colliders.
abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator in the hadronic decay of a boosted boson. We focus on the small-acoplanarity region, where the two hadron momenta are nearly back-to-back in the plane transverse to the boson momentum. We derive a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization formula for electroweak and Higgs bosons in this region, expressed directly in boosted-frame variables in terms of hard, soft, and jet functions with a one-dimensional recoil measurement. We verify its singular real-emission terms at next-to-leading order and present resummed predictions up to N$^3$LL for asymmetric $e^+e^-$ colliders. title: Charge-resolved four-lepton probes of an $e\mu$-flavour-violating scalar at FCC-ee
authors: K. Deka, B. Rawat, T. Srivastava
gist: Proposes charge-resolved four-lepton signatures to probe an e-mu flavour-violating scalar at FCC-ee.
abstract: We study a real neutral scalar $X$ with a single flavour-off-diagonal coupling $h_{e\mu}=h_{\mu e}\equiv h$. The coupling induces associated production, $e^+e^-\to e^\pm\mu^\mp X$, and the decay $X\to e^\pm\mu^\mp$. The resulting four-lepton final state separates into the charge-balanced channel $e^+e^-\mu^+\mu^-$ and the same-sign same-flavour channels $e^\pm e^\pm\mu^\mp\mu^\mp$. The charge-balanced channel receives a large prompt continuum background, while the same-sign category has a small estimated background under our benchmark assumptions. title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
authors: K. Agashe, A. Banerjee, K. Panchal, et al.
gist: Shows that warped extra-dimension models, motivated by the hierarchy problem, can be tested at next-generation dark matter direct detection experiments.
abstract: The coming years will see what could be the final push in the search for WIMP dark matter (DM), with direct detection reaching into the neutrino fog and indirect detection reaching TeV-scale thermal relics. We study a class of models that these experiments could discover: DM emerging from a warped extra dimension. In the IR, these scenarios appear generically as a $Z'$-type portal. We show that DM with electroweak couplings and TeV scale masses remains viable and discoverable within such a bottom-up context. title: Thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation with the Standard Model
authors: M. A. Mojahed
gist: Derives thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation when the inflaton couples to the Standard Model plasma.
abstract: In warm inflation with the Standard Model (SM), an axion-like inflaton dissipates energy into the plasma through QCD sphaleron transitions. Current predictions assume a friction linear in the bias, defined as the free energy released per transition in units of the temperature. The friction, however, has only been simulated at moderate biases in pure SU(2) gauge theory. We show that, during slow roll, energy conservation, the axial anomaly and thermodynamics relate the bias to the quark chemical potentials generated by the transitions, independently of the form of the friction and of the reaction network in the plasma. title: All the Positive Energy Correlators
authors: L. Ricci, M. Riembau, M. Son
gist: Characterises the set of positive energy correlators in QFT, using positivity to derive constraints on the allowed correlator space.
abstract: We develop a framework to systematically obtain the full set of positivity bounds on multi-point energy correlators for sources of arbitrary spin. The constraints are organized in a family of positive operators $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, with $k=0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. Our approach provides outer bounds, which exclude correlators that violate the positivity of $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, and inner bounds, obtained by constructing ensembles of consistent collider events via linear programming. Both methods converge to each other as numerical precision increases. This approach, in particular, characterizes the allowed higher-point correlators once lower-point correlators are determined. title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
authors: Y. F. Bautista, S. De Angelis, D. A. Kosower, et al.
gist: Shows a hidden simplicity in the classical limit of scattering amplitudes, useful for gravitational dynamics and waveform computations.
abstract: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. title: How to Play a Black Hole: Understanding Quasinormal Mode Excitation
authors: L. Vélez-Tartajo, V. Cardoso, J. Redondo-Yuste
gist: Explains how quasinormal modes of black holes are excited, clarifying what determines their amplitudes in the ringdown signal.
abstract: Understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. In this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. In the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
authors: A. Liu, M. Wright, J. Heynen, et al.
gist: Re-examines the claimed evidence for gravitational lensing in the exceptional gravitational-wave event GW231123.
abstract: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. title: Modified recombination or dynamical dark energy (or both)?
authors: A. Reeves, G. P. Lynch, A. Nicola, et al.
gist: Compares modified recombination and dynamical dark energy as explanations of current cosmological tensions, finding what data can distinguish them.
abstract: Several recent analyses report a hint of modified recombination when the latest cosmic microwave background (CMB) and baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data are jointly analysed. We examine whether this preference persists when allowing for departures in the late-time expansion history of the Universe. We fit a seven-parameter reconstruction of the free-electron fraction and a $w_0w_a$ dark-energy model, separately and jointly, to DESI DR2 BAO, a $5\times2$pt combination of galaxy clustering and CMB lensing, and three CMB likelihoods: P-ACT, Planck PR4 and Planck 2018. title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
authors: T. Dzhatdoev, I. Kudryashov, A. Semenov
gist: Tests whether star formation can account for the cosmic-ray proton spectrum from 40 GeV to 10 EeV in a single model.
abstract: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. title: Updated T2K measurement of neutrino oscillation parameters with the first data from the Gadolinium-loaded far detector
authors: The T2K collaboration
gist: Updated T2K neutrino oscillation measurement including the first data with gadolinium-loaded Super-Kamiokande.
abstract: The T2K experiment presents updated measurements of neutrino oscillation parameters using $21.4(16.3)\times10^{20}$ protons on target (POT) in (anti-)neutrino mode at the far detector, Super-Kamiokande. This analysis uses an additional neutrino dataset of $1.7 \times 10^{20}$ POT compared to the previous result, and for the very first time, data collected with Super-Kamiokande doped with Gadolinium (Gd). Significant improvements were introduced in the far detector selection and systematic error treatment. title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
authors: M. C. Bañuls, K. Cichy, C.-J. D. Lin, et al.
gist: Computes parton distribution-like quantities in the Schwinger model with matrix product states, a step toward quantum-simulation approaches to hadron structure.
abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework.
